dossier.purpose:
Playwright (microsoft/playwright, v1.63.0, Apache-2.0) is a TypeScript npm-workspaces monorepo for browser automation and end-to-end web testing: a Node.js library/driver that drives Chromium, Firefox and WebKit through one API, the @playwright/test runner (reporters, HTML report, trace viewer), and agent-facing tooling (an MCP server, a playwright-cli client with installable skills, init-agents/init-skills generators) (README.md:7,25; package.json:54-56; packages/playwright/src/program.ts:161-202; packages/playwright-core/src/cli/program.ts:240-253).

Facts relevant to the three stated needs (whole tree searched at this revision, excluding browser_patches and node_modules):
(1) Labeled-case evaluation with several scorers kept per sample: none found. Grep for scorer/grader/graded/verifier/golden set/promptfoo/inspect_ai/braintrust/deepeval/langsmith finds no evaluation code; the only 'scorer'/'score' hits are selector-ranking code (packages/injected/src/layoutSelectorUtils.ts:64-69, packages/injected/src/selectorGenerator.ts), and 'trial' is the click `trial` option (docs/src/api/params.md:168-171). What the test runner keeps per test and per retry: status, duration, errors, steps, tags, annotations {type, description}, attachments (packages/playwright/src/reporters/json.ts:176-223; tests/config/parquetReporter.ts:69-122). `expect.soft` allows several non-fatal assertions in one test (docs/src/test-assertions-js.md:121-149). No scorer API was found.
(2) Runner for the real Claude Code and Codex CLIs with verifier-graded trials: none found. No spawn/exec of `claude` or `codex`, no `claude -p`, `codex exec` or `@openai/codex` anywhere (grep). `init-agents --loop=claude|codex` only writes agent-definition files (packages/playwright/src/agents/generateAgents.ts:38-150); its tests assert only those files (tests/mcp/init-agents.spec.ts:77-123); MCP tests drive the server with the MCP SDK's own client over stdio (tests/mcp/fixtures.ts:22-23,130-154). No container-based task-suite runner was found.
(3) Declarative CI regression gate for prompts, skills or agents: none found. The repo's own CI uses an LLM only in two GitHub Copilot CLI triage workflows (`--model claude-opus-4.8`) that post a draft comment when the output file is non-empty (.github/workflows/triage.yml:37-69; .github/workflows/pr-ci-triage.yml:42-74). The .claude/skills/* files are maintainer skills (e.g. .claude/skills/playwright-triage/SKILL.md); nothing under .github/workflows checks them.
The project's own gating for browser behaviour is `playwright test`: exit code 0 only when the run status is 'passed', else 1 (130 when interrupted) (packages/playwright/src/cli/testActions.ts:66-107), with options such as --forbid-only, --fail-on-flaky-tests, --max-failures, --last-failed, --only-changed, --shard (packages/playwright/src/program.ts:208-248).

claims.claim: Playwright is a framework for web automation and testing; it drives Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with a single API in tests, in scripts, and as a tool for AI agents.
Playwright Test is a full-featured end-to-end test runner with full browser isolation, auto-waiting and web-first assertions.
Tests run in parallel across all configured browsers, headless by default; each test gets a fresh browser context.
Tracing captures execution traces, screenshots and videos on failure and can be inspected in the Trace Viewer (`trace: 'on-first-retry'`, `npx playwright show-trace trace.zip`).

Playwright CLI is a command-line interface for coding agents (Claude Code, Copilot) and is more token-efficient than MCP because commands avoid loading large tool schemas and accessibility trees into the model context.
`playwright-cli install --skills` installs skills for richer agent integration.
`playwright-cli show` opens a dashboard with live screencast previews of all running browser sessions; a session can be zoomed and remote-controlled.

The Playwright MCP server gives AI agents browser control through structured accessibility snapshots, with no vision models or screenshots required; element refs such as e5/e10 are used to act deterministically.
For Claude Code: `claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest`; the standard mcpServers config works with VS Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf and other MCP clients.
MCP tools cover navigation, form filling, screenshots, network mocking, storage management, and more.
As a library (`npm i playwright`) it supports screenshots, PDF generation, device emulation and network interception without a test runner.
Cross-browser table: Chromium 153.0.8010.12, WebKit 26.6, Firefox 155.0 on Linux, macOS and Windows; headless and headed on all platforms; Chromium uses Chrome for Testing by default.
Playwright is also available for Python, .NET and Java.
The MCP server, the CLI for coding agents and the VS Code extension are linked as separate GitHub repositories (playwright-mcp, playwright-cli, playwright-vscode).

install.method: npm: scaffold a Playwright Test project (README does not distinguish Linux/macOS)
npm: add Playwright Test manually, then download browsers; the docs add `npx playwright install --with-deps` to install Linux OS libraries
npm global: Playwright CLI for coding agents, with optional skills install
npx: Playwright MCP server; Claude Code registration
install.command: npx @playwright/mcp@latest   |   claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest

install.method: Docker image (Linux; Ubuntu 24.04 'noble' tag, also -jammy and -resolute; %%VERSION%% is a docs placeholder for the release version)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes. README table marks Chromium/WebKit/Firefox on Linux (README.md:297-301); docs list Debian 12/13 and Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04, x86-64 or arm64 (docs/src/intro-js.md:308) and say Ubuntu 20.04 is dropped in 1.63 (docs/src/release-notes-js.md:119); registry has x64 downloads for those distros (packages/playwright-core/src/server/registry/index.ts:134-136,144,146,204-206,239-241,249,251); CI runs ubuntu-22.04 (.github/workflows/tests_primary.yml:40) and amd64 Docker images (.github/workflows/tests_docker.yml:16-34). Other distros fall back to ubuntu24.04 builds flagged 'not officially supported' (packages/utils/hostPlatform.ts:122; packages/playwright-core/src/server/registry/index.ts:1101-1102).
platforms.wsl2: yes (WSL is listed; WSL version not stated). docs/src/intro-js.md:306 lists 'Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)'; README.md is silent; the test suite has a 'webkit-wsl' channel (tests/config/browserTest.ts:78) but no WSL job was found in .github/workflows.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes. Docs require macOS 14+ (docs/src/intro-js.md:307); registry has mac14/mac15/mac26 -arm64 builds for Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (packages/playwright-core/src/server/registry/index.ts:158,160,162,228,230,232,263,265,267); Apple CPUs are detected as -arm64 (packages/utils/hostPlatform.ts:67-71); CI uses macos-15-xlarge (Arm64) and macos-14-xlarge, but PR runs of that workflow are label-gated (.github/workflows/tests_secondary.yml:9,25,30-35). WebKit on macOS 14 uses a frozen older revision 2251 (packages/playwright-core/browsers.json:29-32).
platforms.gpu: no (not required). No GPU requirement appears in README or docs; Chromium is launched with --enable-unsafe-swiftshader, a software-GL fallback (packages/playwright-core/src/server/chromium/chromium.ts:377-378); Linux CI uses an xvfb-run virtual display (.github/actions/run-test/action.yml:69-70). No GPU-acceleration feature was found.

integrations.cli: yes. `playwright` bin (packages/playwright/cli.js -> src/program.ts: test, show-report, merge-reports, clear-cache, init-agents, init-skills, hidden test-server and run-test-mcp-server) and `playwright-core` bin (packages/playwright-core/cli.js) with core commands open, codegen, install, uninstall, install-deps, screenshot, pdf, show-trace, trace, cli, mcp (packages/playwright-core/src/cli/program.ts:37-254; packages/playwright/src/program.ts:40-257). The playwright-cli client code is packages/playwright-core/src/tools/cli-client/program.ts (run in-repo as `npx playwright cli` or `npm run playwright-cli`, package.json:51); README names the standalone @playwright/cli package from a separate repo (README.md:113-118,155).
integrations.mcp: yes. MCP server in this repo: `npx playwright mcp` (packages/playwright-core/src/cli/program.ts:251-253; packages/playwright-core/src/tools/mcp/program.ts:33-163), stdio by default and HTTP/SSE with --port (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/utils/mcp/http.ts:38-100). A second MCP server exposes the test runner: hidden `run-test-mcp-server` (packages/playwright/src/program.ts:140-159; tools test_list, test_run, test_debug, planner_*, generator_* in packages/playwright/src/mcp/test/). README directs users to the separate @playwright/mcp package (README.md:161,172,208).
integrations.sdk_or_api: yes. Node.js/TypeScript library API (`playwright`, `playwright-core`, `@playwright/test`; README.md:212-273; packages/*/package.json exports) with public types generated from docs/src (CONTRIBUTING.md:40). Other-language bindings talk to a Node driver over stdio (`run-driver`) or WebSocket (`run-server`, `launch-server`) (packages/playwright-core/src/cli/program.ts:172-205; packages/playwright-core/src/cli/driver.ts:30-95). MCP HTTP/SSE transport as above.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Claude Code: documented. `claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest` (README.md:185; docs/src/getting-started-mcp.md:53-57); `npx playwright init-agents --loop=claude` writes .claude/agents/*.md and .mcp.json (docs/src/test-agents-js.md:38-40; packages/playwright/src/agents/generateAgents.ts:38-62; tests/mcp/init-agents.spec.ts:77-92); skills via `playwright-cli install --skills` into .claude/skills (docs/src/getting-started-cli.md:39-49; packages/playwright-core/src/tools/utils/installSkills.ts:25-41) or `npx playwright init-skills` (packages/playwright/src/program.ts:187-202; tests/mcp/init-agents.spec.ts:125-142); CLI help prints the skill path when env CLAUDECODE or COPILOT_CLI is set (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/cli-client/program.ts:108-111). Codex: `npx playwright init-agents --loop=codex` writes .codex/agents/*.toml with sandbox_mode and an MCP server entry (docs/src/test-agents-js.md:42-44; generateAgents.ts:94-150; tests/mcp/init-agents.spec.ts:94-123); Codex is listed among MCP clients that accept the standard config (docs/src/getting-started-mcp.md:65). `--loop agents` installs skills to .agents/skills, not stated to be Codex-specific (installSkills.ts:28; program.ts:190-192). In every case Playwright generates configuration or serves tools; no code launches either CLI (grep).

readme.telemetry_and_network: README.md is silent on telemetry. No telemetry/analytics/usage-reporting code was found: grep over packages/ for telemetry|analytics|appinsights returns only a Firefox pref string (packages/playwright-core/src/server/bidi/third_party/firefoxPrefs.ts:129); that BiDi Firefox pref set disables health-report and data upload (firefoxPrefs.ts:123-133); Chromium launch switches include --disable-background-networking, --disable-component-update, --metrics-recording-only, --disable-sync (packages/playwright-core/src/server/chromium/chromiumSwitches.ts:53-96). Required network: `npx playwright install` downloads browser archives over HTTPS from cdn.playwright.dev and playwright.download.prss.microsoft.com (packages/playwright-core/src/server/registry/index.ts:47-51,117-126); the request User-Agent carries Playwright version, CPU arch, OS id/version, Node version and a CI/1 flag (packages/playwright-core/src/server/userAgent.ts:36-65; packages/playwright-core/src/server/registry/oopDownloadBrowserMain.ts:55-60). Overrides: PLAYWRIGHT_DOWNLOAD_HOST and per-browser hosts (registry/index.ts:1082-1095), PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD (registry/index.ts:1335-1339). Otherwise network use is whatever the automated pages and the user's LLM client do. Accounts: README/getting-started docs require no account or API key; CI-side Azure/GitHub secrets are maintainer-only (.github/actions/run-test/action.yml:83-95). Optional hosted viewer: trace.playwright.dev is linked from the trace-viewer UI (packages/trace-viewer/src/ui/workbenchLoader.tsx:214) and deployed by publish_release.yml:49-83. Local services: MCP HTTP binds localhost by default (packages/utils/network.ts:239-245) and `run-server` defaults to localhost (packages/utils/wsServer.ts:64-69). `playwright-cli`/MCP output under .playwright-cli/ may contain credentials; the CLI patches .gitignore with that warning (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/cli-daemon/program.ts:115-129).

languages: JavaScript (CLI shims, utils/*.js, Firefox juggler patch in browser_patches/firefox)
TSX/React and CSS (html-reporter, trace-viewer, recorder, dashboard, web, extension UIs)
Shell (docker, publish and emulator scripts under utils/)

entry_points.what: `playwright` binary; loads lib/program (src/program.ts): test, show-report, merge-reports, clear-cache, init-agents, init-skills, hidden test-server and run-test-mcp-server.

`playwright-core` binary; decorates a commander program with core commands (src/cli/program.ts): open, codegen, install, uninstall, install-deps, screenshot, pdf, show-trace, trace, cli, mcp, hidden run-driver/run-server/launch-server.
`playwright mcp` command: Playwright MCP server (stdio, or HTTP/SSE with --port); options include --caps, --extension, --cdp-endpoint, --secrets, --allowed-hosts.
Lines 140-159: hidden `run-test-mcp-server` (MCP server over the test runner); lines 161-202: init-agents and init-skills commands.
`playwright-cli` client (sessions registry, talks to the daemon in tools/cli-daemon/); run as `npx playwright cli` or `npm run playwright-cli`.
runDriver (stdio protocol for non-Node language bindings), runServer (WebSocket server), launchBrowserServer.
init-agents generators for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode and VS Code, built from the planner/generator/healer .agent.md files in the same directory.
`playwright trace` subcommands (open, actions, action, requests, console, errors, snapshot, screenshot, attachments, install-skill) for inspecting trace.zip from the command line.

code.architecture: npm-workspaces monorepo (package.json:54-56); TypeScript compiled and bundled by esbuild into per-package lib/ (utils/build/build.js:643-713; .claude/skills/playwright-dev/vendor.md:9-64). Client/server split over an RPC protocol (.claude/skills/playwright-dev/library.md:1-90): protocol spec packages/protocol/spec/*.yml generates validators/channels (packages/protocol/src); client API objects in packages/playwright-core/src/client/; browser automation in packages/playwright-core/src/server/ with engine backends chromium/, firefox/, webkit/, bidi/, android/, electron/, dispatchers in server/dispatchers/, browser download and registry in server/registry/, remote WebSocket server in src/remote/; shared code in packages/isomorphic/ and packages/utils/; in-page scripts in packages/injected/. Test runner in packages/playwright/src/{runner,worker,common,matchers,reporters,transform,plugins,cli}/ (built-in reporters list, line, dot, json, junit, null, github, html, blob, perfetto: packages/playwright/src/common/config.ts:292). Agent/MCP tooling in packages/playwright-core/src/tools/{backend (capability-gated browser_* tools), mcp, cli-client, cli-daemon, dashboard, trace, skills (SKILL.md files), utils}; test-agent definitions and generators in packages/playwright/src/agents/; test-runner MCP in packages/playwright/src/mcp/test/. UIs: packages/{html-reporter,trace-viewer,recorder,web,dashboard,extension}. Import boundaries enforced by 51 DEPS.list files under packages/ via utils/check_deps.js (CLAUDE.md:86-91; `npm run lint`, package.json:38). Browser-engine patches live in browser_patches/{firefox,webkit,winldd}; public API types are generated from docs/src (CLAUDE.md:31).
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts: 10 public npm packages: playwright, playwright-core, @playwright/test, playwright-chromium/-firefox/-webkit, @playwright/browser-chromium/-firefox/-webkit (utils/workspace.js:144-197; @playwright/client is private, packages/playwright-client/package.json:3), built by `npm run build`; Docker images pushed to playwright.azurecr.io/public/playwright for Ubuntu jammy/noble/resolute x amd64/arm64 (utils/docker/publish_docker.sh:29-150; docs/src/docker.md:21 pulls from mcr.microsoft.com); trace viewer deployed to trace.playwright.dev (.github/workflows/publish_release.yml:49-83); Chrome extension uploaded to the Chrome Web Store (.github/workflows/publish_extension.yml:1-76); browser binaries served from cdn.playwright.dev (registry/index.ts:47-51). Release flow: .github/workflows/publish_release.yml publishes @next (daily cron or manual, alpha versions), @beta (pushes to release-*) and @latest (GitHub release published) using npm OIDC login (`id-token: write`, lines 5-10,18-20,30-47) through utils/publish_all_packages.sh (`npm publish --access=public ... --tag`, line 80). A manual Azure pipeline .azure-pipelines/publish.yml packs with `npm pack` and releases through the EsrpRelease@11 task with signcertname 'ESRP-Release-Sign' (lines 125-169); .azure-pipelines/publish-docker.yml builds and pushes Docker images on v* tags. Version consistency is checked by `utils/workspace.js --ensure-consistent` (workspace.js:80-139,212-220). Integrity: no checksum files, cosign/sigstore signatures, SBOM or explicit npm `--provenance` flag were found in .github, .azure-pipelines or utils (grep); the Docker build sets BUILDX_NO_DEFAULT_ATTESTATIONS=1 (utils/docker/build.sh:45-46); images get an oras 'lifecycle end-of-life' artifact, which is not a signature (publish_docker.sh:70-77). Published packages ship per-bundle *.LICENSE sidecars (packages/playwright-core/.npmignore:7-8; packages/playwright-core/ThirdPartyNotices.txt:5-11).
code.tests_and_ci: Frameworks: the repo dogfoods Playwright Test (package.json:19-35). Spec-file counts (files containing test code): tests/page 134 (page+server fixtures), tests/library 156, tests/playwright-test 98 (run with a pinned prior @playwright/test via `npm run ttest`, package.json:30; tests/playwright-test/stable-test-runner/package.json:4), tests/mcp 95 (MCP SDK client over stdio, tests/mcp/fixtures.ts:22-23), tests/installation 21, tests/extension 6, tests/android 5, tests/electron 4, tests/stress 2; tests/bidi and tests/webview have configs/expectations but no spec files of their own; plus 10 spec files under packages/ (html-reporter, web, skill templates). About 525 spec files under tests/ in total (a regex count of about 10.7k `test(`/`it(` lines is only an upper bound because tests/playwright-test embeds test sources in strings). CI reporters: dot, json, blob, parquet-to-DuckDB (tests/library/playwright.config.ts:46-55); CI sets retries 3 and forbidOnly for library and installation suites (tests/library/playwright.config.ts:68-69; tests/installation/playwright.config.ts:42,45). Workflows (.github/workflows, 19 YAML files): tests_primary.yml 'tests 1' (library tests per browser on ubuntu-22.04 Node 20, plus chromium on Node 22/24 and ubuntu arm64; `ttest` sharded on ubuntu/macOS/windows Node 20-26; html-reporter/web component tests; playwright-vscode extension tests; install tests; clock tests; PRs skip docs/tools/mcp/bidi/extension paths, lines 8-20); tests_secondary.yml 'tests 2' (macOS, Windows, driver, tracing, Chrome/Edge channels, Android emulator, Electron, install tests on Node 20/24/26; PR runs only when labeled CQ1, lines 9,25); tests_mcp.yml (`npm run test-mcp` on ubuntu/macOS/windows x chrome/chromium/firefox/webkit/msedge); tests_bidi.yml (nightly plus bidi PRs); tests_docker.yml/_changes/_release (jammy/noble/resolute x amd64/arm64, `@smoke` tests inside containers); tests_extension.yml (macOS); tests_webview_simulator.yml (iOS simulator, 4 shards); infra.yml (`npm run lint` = eslint, tsc, doclint, check-deps, generate_channels, generate_types, lint-tests, test-types, lint-packages; clean-tree check; non-blocking `npm audit` with continue-on-error; snippet lint for Python/.NET/Java); create_test_report.yml (merge blob reports, PR comment and commit status, Copilot-based CI triage on failures); update_test_results_db.yml (DuckDB ingest every 3 hours); publish/roll/triage/copilot-setup workflows. Also 4 composite actions (.github/actions) and 2 Azure pipelines (.azure-pipelines).
code.dependencies: Root package.json: no `dependencies`, 109 pinned `devDependencies` (package.json:57-166), vendored/bundled into lib/ at build time (utils/build/build.js:675-713; .claude/skills/playwright-dev/vendor.md:9-35). code.security_policy: SECURITY.md (Microsoft MSRC template): report privately via https://msrc.microsoft.com/create-report or secure@microsoft.com, not via public issues; coordinated vulnerability disclosure (SECURITY.md:9-39).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:7 - drives Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with a single API in tests, scripts and as a tool for AI agents.
claim_checks.evidence: Engine backends exist in packages/playwright-core/src/server/chromium/chromium.ts, firefox/firefox.ts, webkit/webkit.ts; test runner command in packages/playwright/src/program.ts:40-78; agent tooling in packages/playwright-core/src/tools/mcp/program.ts:33-163, tools/cli-client/program.ts and packages/playwright/src/program.ts:161-202.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:63,105 - tests run in parallel across configured browsers, headless by default, each test with a fresh browser context.
claim_checks.evidence: Headless defaults to true (packages/playwright/src/index.ts:213) and the `context` fixture creates a context per test unless reuse mode is on (index.ts:469-480); default workers are 50% of cores (packages/playwright/src/common/config.ts:110). Code/docs differ from the 'parallel by default' wording: only test files run in parallel by default, tests inside one file run in order in one worker unless fullyParallel (docs/src/test-parallel-js.md:8; --fully-parallel default false at packages/playwright/src/program.ts:215).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:88-101 - tracing captures traces, screenshots and videos on failure, viewable with show-trace.
claim_checks.evidence: Trace modes include retain-on-failure and on-first-retry (packages/playwright/src/program.ts:204); video retention logic (packages/playwright/src/index.ts:542-566) and screenshot on-failure modes (index.ts:624-672); `show-trace` command (packages/playwright-core/src/cli/program.ts:207-236). It is opt-in: trace, screenshot and video default to 'off' (index.ts:81-82,219). An agent-facing `playwright trace` CLI also exists (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/trace/traceCli.ts:35-147).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:113 - Playwright CLI is more token-efficient than MCP.
claim_checks.evidence: No measurement, benchmark or token count exists in the repo (grep: the claim appears only as prose at README.md:113 and docs/src/getting-started-cli.md:8,12). Design evidence only: CLI output references a snapshot file under .playwright-cli/ instead of inlining it (docs/src/getting-started-cli.md:85-93; packages/playwright-core/src/tools/skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md:277), whereas MCP tools return the snapshot (docs/src/getting-started-mcp.md:81).

Handled in packages/playwright-core/src/tools/cli-client/program.ts:204-208,330 and tools/cli-daemon/program.ts:47-48,89-109; skills playwright-cli, playwright-component-testing, playwright-trace are copied to .claude/skills or .agents/skills (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/utils/installSkills.ts:25-41). The standalone @playwright/cli package is published from a different repo (README.md:113,155) and was not inspected; the same code runs here as `npx playwright cli` (packages/playwright-core/src/cli/program.ts:240-249).

claim_checks.evidence: The `show` command (with --port, --host, --annotate, --kill) is declared at packages/playwright-core/src/tools/cli-daemon/commands.ts:1034-1048 and the dashboard server is packages/playwright-core/src/tools/dashboard/dashboardApp.ts; live screencast and remote-control behaviour was not executed or read in detail.

risks: Scope: at this revision the repo contains no evaluation harness (no scorers, datasets or per-sample score storage), no runner for the real Claude Code/Codex CLIs, and no CI gate for prompts/skills/agents (grep, see purpose). Its agent features are config generators (packages/playwright/src/agents/generateAgents.ts:38-150), an MCP server and CLI/skills tooling (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/); its own CI LLM use is two Copilot-CLI triage workflows that only check for a non-empty draft (.github/workflows/triage.yml:65-69).

Security (MCP): `browser_run_code_unsafe` is described as 'RCE-equivalent' (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/backend/runCode.ts:30-37) yet sits in capability 'core', so it is in the default tool list (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/backend/tools.ts:79-80; tests/mcp/capabilities.spec.ts:19-47); docs say 'only enable it for trusted MCP clients' (docs/src/getting-started-mcp.md:106) but no option to disable it appears in the `mcp` flags (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/mcp/program.ts:35-82). The HTTP/SSE transport has no authentication, only a localhost bind and Host-header allow-list against DNS rebinding (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/utils/mcp/http.ts:61-83), and --host 0.0.0.0 is allowed (mcp/program.ts:55). --allowed-origins/--blocked-origins are documented as not a security boundary (mcp/program.ts:36,38) and --secrets as 'a convenience and not a security feature' (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/mcp/config.d.ts:149-154). File access is restricted to the workspace by default (mcp/program.ts:37).

Security (browsers): Chromium is launched with --no-sandbox unless chromiumSandbox is true (packages/playwright-core/src/server/chromium/chromium.ts:389-390; docs/src/api/params.md:1150-1152). The Chrome extension requests debugger, tabs, activeTab, tabGroups and <all_urls> host permissions (packages/extension/manifest.json:6-14) and lets an MCP client reuse the user's logged-in profile (packages/extension/README.md:5,45-72). CLI/MCP artifacts under .playwright-cli/ may contain credentials (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/cli-daemon/program.ts:124).

Integrity/supply chain: downloaded browser archives are checked only by byte count (and only when not chunked), with no hash or signature verification (packages/playwright-core/src/server/registry/oopDownloadBrowserMain.ts:84-92); no checksum, signature, SBOM or explicit npm provenance flag was found in the release workflows (.github/workflows/publish_release.yml:30-47; utils/publish_all_packages.sh:80), and Docker builds disable buildx default attestations (utils/docker/build.sh:45-46). Browser binaries are separate third-party artifacts from the project CDN (registry/index.ts:47-51), not covered by the repo LICENSE.

Agent-feature stability and failure masking: the generated healer agent is instructed to edit failing tests until they pass and to mark them test.fixme() when confident the test is correct (packages/playwright/src/agents/playwright-test-healer.agent.md:36-55; docs/src/test-agents-js.md:213), which converts failures into passes or skips. The `--run-agents` option is declared (packages/playwright/src/program.ts:234) but no other reference to it exists in the repo. Agent definitions must be regenerated on each Playwright upgrade (docs/src/test-agents-js.md:30-32) and the Copilot spec hardcodes a model name (generateAgents.ts:266).

Platform/version drift: docs say Node.js 'latest 22.x, 24.x or 26.x' (docs/src/intro-js.md:305) while package.json engines is >=20 (package.json:11-13) and CI still runs Node 20 (.github/workflows/tests_primary.yml:41). Official platforms are macOS 14+, Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04, Debian 12/13 (docs/src/intro-js.md:303-308); Ubuntu 20.04 was dropped in 1.63 (docs/src/release-notes-js.md:119); other Linux distros get fallback builds flagged unsupported (packages/utils/hostPlatform.ts:122); WSL is listed without a version (intro-js.md:306); WebKit on macOS 14 is frozen at an older revision (packages/playwright-core/browsers.json:29-32).

Dependency and CI hygiene: 109 pinned devDependencies bundled at build time (package.json:57-166); `npm audit` in CI is non-blocking (.github/workflows/infra.yml:33-35); the test-runner suite depends on a pinned alpha of @playwright/test (tests/playwright-test/stable-test-runner/package.json:4); PR runs of the macOS/Windows/Android/Electron workflow happen only with the CQ1 label (.github/workflows/tests_secondary.yml:9,25); create_test_report.yml waits on a workflow named 'tests others' that no workflow defines (.github/workflows/create_test_report.yml:4). CONTRIBUTING.md states PRs without a linked, approved issue, or low-quality agent-generated PRs, are closed (CONTRIBUTING.md:5-16).

Licensing: repository is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE; package.json:17) with code derived from Puppeteer, also Apache-2.0 (NOTICE:4-5) and 'Portions Copyright 2017 Google Inc.' (LICENSE:190). Bundled npm dependencies keep their own licenses in per-bundle *.LICENSE sidecars (packages/playwright-core/ThirdPartyNotices.txt:5-11; .claude/skills/playwright-dev/vendor.md:73-80); third-party code also sits under packages/playwright-core/src/server/bidi/third_party/ (own LICENSE) and packages/web/src/third_party/vscode/ (LICENSE.txt). Licenses of the downloaded browser builds are not in this repo.

checks.statement: npm: add Playwright Test manually, then download browsers: `npm i -D @playwright/test` then `npx playwright install`; the docs add `npx playwright install --with-deps` to install Linux OS libraries.
checks.note: README.md:36-37 contains exactly `npm i -D @playwright/test` / `npx playwright install`. The `install` command and its `--with-deps` option ('install system dependencies for browsers') are defined at packages/playwright-core/src/cli/program.ts:76-78. browsers.md:119-122 says combining install-deps with install installs 'the browsers and OS dependencies' in one command and shows `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`. Minor narrowing: the cited docs say 'OS dependencies', not Linux. In code, install-deps installs distro packages on Linux, runs install_media_pack.ps1 for Chromium on Windows, and does nothing on macOS (packages/playwright-core/src/server/registry/index.ts:928-931; registry/dependencies.ts:78-92). 'Linux OS libraries' is accurate for Linux and does not misstate the commands.

LICENSE:1-2 is the Apache License, Version 2.0, with appendix 'Portions Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. / Portions Copyright 2017 Google Inc.' (LICENSE:189-190). The root package.json:17 and every packages/*/package.json (e.g. playwright:51, playwright-core:16, playwright-test:16, browser packages:16) declare "Apache-2.0". NOTICE:4-5 credits Puppeteer-derived code, also Apache 2.0.
